lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: Maps. Maps are the only true thing left in Hollowmere. Floors stop pretending when you draw them.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: Every wardens' map the town ever owned burned in the mine office. I am rebuilding them one descent at a time.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: Want? I need them. Bring me back enough rope-ends and I will give you something better than directions — I will give you the shape of the dark.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: And I will make it worth your while. The old surveyors' kit is still in my cellar, and nobody else alive knows the lock pattern.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: The Foreman is done? Then let me mark it properly — big red cross, the kind the old charts used.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: You know what the old charts never marked? Where the Foreman's crew actually went. Every map ends at the same gallery and then just... stops.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: I think the mine did. Eleven miners do not all forget how to walk home at once.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: Find the place where they stopped and draw it. That is all I ask. The truth keeps better in ink than in rumors.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: The miners are walking up and my maps are wrong. Not torn, not burned. Wrong. The shafts they climb were never on any chart I own.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: Count the lanterns. I will count them too. If we get the same number, I will believe my own eyes for once.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: I have started drawing floors nobody has descended yet. I do not know where the habit came from.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: The ink keeps moving after I set it down. I have decided not to look at the wet ones.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: Every map has an edge. Even the deep ones. Even yours.

lines.speaker: Pip
lines.text: Back so soon? The ink is not even dry on your last route.
